story.head: Nichushkin meets his old team
paras: The Blue Jackets (5-7-0) lost 3-1 to Dallas on Saturday, while the Avalanche have won two in a row. The Avalanche played last night, and the Blue Jackets are rested. Going in, the Avalanche are third in the Central (tied for 13th in the NHL) and the Blue Jackets last in the Metropolitan (tied for 29th).

The Avalanche’s record (.607) is about what their chances are worth. The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.417) says: their chances are worth about .482, and their finishing has held them back.

The Avalanche (2nd) and the Blue Jackets (5th) both get their defensemen shooting. The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest) and play the league’s fastest games (1st). Colorado has scored 4.21 goals a game, the most in the league. As for the Blue Jackets, they keep things calm after the whistle (5th lowest). They also have a leaky penalty kill (30th), so the Avs kill penalties well, but them don’t. Columbus has scored 2.33 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league.

Nathan MacKinnon (9 G / 15 A / 24 P in 14 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is tied for fourth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. Artturi Lehkonen (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 14 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for second in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (7 G / 5 A / 12 P in 12 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Zach Werenski (0 G / 10 A / 10 P in 12 GP) isn’t far behind.
Scott Wedgewood (1-2-1 / .889 SV% in 4 GS) will likely start for Colorado, and Cam Talbot (3-2-0 / .893 SV% in 5 GS) for Columbus.

At home, Rick Bowness likes to send Sillinger, Monahan and Garland out against opponents’ third lines, so watch for them against Landeskog, Nelson and Roy. Elsewhere, the Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Blue Jackets do.
